title: Creator Fellowship Curriculum Kit
eyebrow: Subject Medias · creator fellowship · the first eight weeks
lead_html: The fellowship's first eight weeks, seat by seat: what a fellow learns, does and shows before they can join a region's crew pool, as Milanote cards. Copy a card here and paste it onto a fellow's board.
footer_html: Built from the TOJ app's fellowship guide and the Pylon crew rules (Nov 12, 2026). The weeks and the sign-offs are proposed: they're confirmed when an approver approves the kit.

source.title: TOJ app guides: fellowship applications, Pylon events (the crew rules)

columns.name: Start here
columns.lead: Who the fellowship is for, and the rules nobody breaks.

cards.title: What the fellowship is
cards.body:
Creators apply on subjectmedias.com/fellowship. Kyron reviews, talks with them, and approves the ones who fit. An approved fellow starts a plan, signs the creator agreement, gets screened, and works a first stop.

The plans: Tools + Community ($29 a month), or Community + 2 Meetings a Week ($79 a month).

cards.title: The rules nobody breaks
cards.body:
1. Real moments only. No AI-made athletes, no synthetic edits of a real one, and no words put in anyone's mouth.
  2. No release, no camera. Consent is confirmed before anyone is filmed. Close or identifying shots of a minor (a face, a readable number) are for their family only, never public. Anything public shows a minor only wide and non-identifying (no face, name or jersey number), and only with a parent's or guardian's verified yes, recorded by staff. Texas youth: Kyron and counsel decide before the first Texas event.
  3. No promises. Nothing says or suggests an offer, a scholarship, a roster spot, exposure, followers or paid work.
  4. No marks you don't own. No NFL marks, broadcast footage or team logos you don't have the right to use, and no school logos on minors.
  5. Never alone with a minor. No locker rooms, training rooms or changing areas, and no one-to-one filming without a parent there.
  6. A pulled consent means pulled footage. When a family takes consent back, it comes down everywhere within 72 hours, at every event.
  7. Nothing publishes without the approver. Nothing goes public without an approver's OK.
  8. 16 or 17: shadow, shooter or photographer only. Never a lead, never an editor, always beside a confirmed, screened adult on site.
  9. No screening, no crew: a contract, a background check and minor-safety training, each less than a year old at the event.
  10. A fellow's footage stays in GFS storage. A fellow never posts, keeps or shares footage they shot: not on their own accounts, not in a portfolio. Reviews happen in the app.
  11. Never messaging or selling to a family as a youth creator.

cards.title: The seats
cards.body:
• Shadow: on site, learning, beside an adult. 16 or older.
  • Shooter: a wide angle or the game's coverage. 16 or older.
  • Photographer: stills. 16 or older.
  • Story camera: the story angle. An adult.
  • Lead: runs a crew. An adult.
  • Editor: after the stop. An adult.

columns.name: Weeks 1 and 2
columns.lead: The rules and the run sheet, before a camera comes out.

cards.title: Week 1: the rules
cards.body:
• Read the Pylon crew rules and the consent flags: who can be clipped, sold, shown publicly, posted.
  • Minor-safety training, if it isn't on file yet.
  • Shows: can say, in their own words, what a keep-out means on the day.

cards.title: Week 2: a stop on paper
cards.body:
• Walk the twelve stages of a stop's run sheet with a lead.
  • Read a crew brief: the pre-sold athletes, the athletes no clip may feature, the naming.
  • Shows: names a game folder and three clips the Schedule B way.

columns.name: Weeks 3 to 5
columns.lead: On site as a shadow, then the craft of each seat.

cards.title: Week 3: shadow a stop
cards.body:
• A full stop beside the lead: set-up, both wide angles, the midday upload check.
  • Shows: a short written debrief of what the lead did and why.

cards.title: Week 4: the wide angle (shooter)
cards.body:
• Sideline and End Zone, full games at 1080p60.
  • Holding a frame for a whole game: framing, exposure, battery and card changes between series.
  • Shows: one full game, both angles, nothing missed.

cards.title: Week 4: stills (photographer)
cards.body:
• The moment and the light, wide enough to read the play. The frames stay in GFS storage for review: a fellow never posts or keeps them.
  • Candid between plays, never staged.
  • Shows: 40 frames from one game, culled to the best 12.

cards.title: Week 5: names, uploads, tags
cards.body:
• Folders and clip names to Schedule B.
  • Every file uploaded within 12 hours of its final whistle.
  • How tag review works, and why a director's call is never overridden.
  • Shows: a clean upload log for a game they shot.

columns.name: Weeks 6 to 8
columns.lead: Working a stop in a seat, and the sign-off.

cards.title: Weeks 6 and 7: a seat at a stop
cards.body:
• Crewed in their seat at a stop, beside a confirmed, screened adult (always, at 16 or 17).
  • The lead rates the work on the day: angles held, files named, uploads on time.

cards.title: Week 8: the sign-off
cards.body: Kyron and the lead look at the work from weeks 4 to 7. A fellow who's ready is put in the region's crew pool for their seat. One who isn't gets the next two weeks' work, named.

cards.title: Adults: the next seats
cards.body: An adult fellow who has held a seat well can learn the story camera, then the lead's job, then the edit. Each starts with shadowing that seat at a stop.

columns.name: Checklists
columns.lead: A fellow's tick-lists, and the sources.

cards.title: Before the first stop
items: Screening on file: contract, background check, minor-safety training
At 16 or 17: guardian's consent on file

cards.title: Sign-off: Kyron and the lead
items: A full game held from both wide angles, or 12 strong stills
Files named and uploaded on time
No clip of a held athlete
The rules, in their own words
Ready for the pool, or the next two weeks named

cards.title: Sources
cards.body: The TOJ app's guides Fellowship applications and Pylon events in the TOJ app (the crew and youth-creator rules), checked Nov 12, 2026. The weeks, the work each one shows and the sign-off are TOJ's proposed curriculum.
